files_read: directory listing (the probe sources, witness transcripts, and three generated per-item reports are named in the writeup and were not read in full; the writeup is the prose that reports the incident)
symptom: The summary banner at the top of every generated per-item report printed a clean pass — a verdict of GREEN, twelve of twelve subsystems, no tensions — on items whose own report, further down the same page, carried a severe alert and a provenance line stating that the grid the assessment leaned on was zero percent authored. Both lines came out of the same run over the same record. Nothing was malformed and no gate objected; the contradiction was simply two statements in one document, one of which is the one a reader takes as the answer.
mechanism_as_described: The banner builder consumed exactly one field of the enriched record — a base verdict from one subsystem — and nothing else. The alerts and the provenance markers were computed, serialized, and printed elsewhere in the same document, but no operation combined them with the headline, so there was no path by which severe evidence could reach the line that summarizes. The headline was therefore not false about its own input: it was a true statement about one subsystem, occupying the position where a reader takes a whole-document verdict. The document names the shape in its own in-house vocabulary: a token that carries the appearance of a result, standing at the read site where the provenance marker belongs.
detection_path: No gate caught it and none could have: the document validated, the run was green, and the two contradicting statements sat far apart in one file. It surfaced when an external review pass read a generated report end to end and noticed the clean banner beside the severe alert. The repair then needed a prior question settled — which inputs may legitimately move a headline — and that was settled by a read-only probe rather than by argument: assert a fully synthetic authored grid across every interval, clear the memo caches, recompute, and see what moves. Nothing moved (0 of 48 summaries changed), and the probe carried its own positive control showing the synthetic grid was live and visible to a different consumer (46 of 46 interval confidences shifted low to high), plus a verified restore leaving no probe facts behind. A null result from a probe that had been shown capable of moving something is what licensed gating the headline on alerts rather than on grid provenance, and tagging grid-fed findings conditional instead.
consequence: Eight of 48 items changed headline once the combining step landed — six from pass to fail, two from warn to fail — which is to say those eight had been publishing a clean summary over their own severe alerts for as long as the banner existed, and the count is corpus-relative rather than a property of the code. The repair adds the combined verdict as a sibling field, leaving the original byte-unchanged for existing consumers, and makes staleness visible: an artifact generated before the change renders an explicit unjoined marker instead of quietly showing the old headline. One floor in the new scheme has never fired on real data — every carrier of the middle grade was already at or above the level that floor would impose — so that path is confirmed conservative and simultaneously unexercised, which the document states rather than leaves implicit.

extraction_notes.boundary_rule_applied: UNIT — prose REPORTS an instance, in a section headed as the defect, quoting the offending banner text and naming where it was observed. The document's subject is the repair, but the incident is stated as an occurrence with a witness, not as a category of risk.
extraction_notes.selection_rule_applied: One incident per directory, fullest DESCRIBED mechanism. Extracted the headline-over-its-own-evidence defect. NOT extracted: (a) a counting bug inside the change's own pre-output gate — the first run of the histogram counted 50 rows over a 48-item corpus because it took all solutions where the serializer takes only the first, corrected in the same pass and recorded in the script; a genuine second instance, one sentence of mechanism; (b) a witness the plan had predicted which turned out to grade differently than predicted, so a different item had to be substituted — the document flags this as witnessed-not-predicted and treats the substitution as itself a correctness signal, so it is a prediction corrected by execution rather than a defect; (c) a conditional tag that is unreachable on the live data by construction, declared as a known edge that will fire when a partially authored grid first exists. (a) is the nearest competitor.
extraction_notes.redaction_note: Predicate, module, and file names, the tracker identifiers, commit hashes, category and alert names, and item identifiers are stripped from the coder-facing fields. The verdict words GREEN/pass/fail, the counts, and the 8-of-48 blast radius are retained; the arithmetic of what changed is the consequence.

metadata.incident_location_note: The document is a close-out for the repair, and opens with a section headed as the defect. The incident is the reason the work exists, though the bulk of the document is what landed rather than what went wrong.
